title: Natural acyclic Cartan--Eilenberg augmentation
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories, and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be left exact additive functors, with $F$ sending injectives to $G$-acyclics [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. For every Cartan--Eilenberg presentation $P$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], there is a quasi-isomorphism $a_P:GF(J_P)\to\operatorname{Tot}G(I_P)$, with the source extended by zero to integer degrees [def-sp-double-complex-total]. In degree $n\ge0$ its component is the common augmentation into the $(n,0)$ total summand, with the canonical extension isomorphisms. These maps are natural for presentation comparisons: $GF(\beta) a_Q=a_P\operatorname{Tot}G(\alpha)$. Negative source terms are zero, so the prescribed components determine the map uniquely.

source.place: Tags 015N (Grothendieck spectral sequence), 015J (CE spectral sequences), 015K (functoriality); acyclic-column argument

proof.text: Construct the augmentation explicitly in every integer degree. Apply G to the bicomplex augmentation, using singleMapHomologicalComplex to identify its source with single degree zero of GF(J). Extend each mapped column by zero. Insert its degree-zero augmentation into the (n,0) total summand. The cochain equation follows from the horizontal augmentation square and from the vanishing vertical composite; the horizontal total sign is one. Compose with the inverse mapExtendIso for F followed by G to get the required extended source. The component calculation uses the explicit inverse component of mapExtendIso. No data is chosen from an existence theorem.

For each integer horizontal degree s, the term of the extended injective resolution is injective, including negative degrees where it is zero. The composite acyclicity hypothesis therefore makes F of that term G-acyclic. The source column is concentrated in vertical degree zero; its other terms are zero and hence G-acyclic. All target column terms are injective by term_injective and therefore G-acyclic. Apply the natural-indexed version of the Leray quasi-isomorphism preservation lemma to column_quasiIso. Precomposition by the single-complex comparison isomorphism gives quasi-isomorphisms for the mapped augmentation columns.

The mapped columns vanish in horizontal degrees below zero. Compose the constructed total augmentation with totalFlipIso.inv. Its (0,n) component is the component required by cartanEilenberg_augmentation_quasiIso because the symmetry sign at (n,0) is one. Apply the exact augmented columns theorem, then cancel the total symmetry isomorphism to obtain a quasi-isomorphism to the unflipped total. Precomposition by the mapExtendIso inverse preserves this property.

Prove naturality for the column total augmentation degreewise using the total-map coprojection identity and extendMap_f. Apply G to Comparison.comm_e to supply the required degree-zero square. Naturality of mapExtendIso then transports that square to the prescribed extended GF source. The calculation holds in every integer degree and consequently covers all negative source terms without a separate choice.
